source.title: Learned Structure Shows Up Earlier in the Task's Own Basis: A Controlled Look at a Synchronisation Precursor in Grokking

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. The text notes that this version withdraws analyses and claims from earlier versions; those withdrawn results are not treated as results of this study.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether a different progress measure, FSDgen, signals learned structure before grokking and whether its timing predicts grokking, rather than reproducing the original mechanistic progress measures.
record.gate_note: The study reports FSDgen synchronization and timing results on modular multiplication and finite-group tasks. It does not directly identify a generalizing circuit, track removal of a memorizing circuit, or test training-set-size effects. The earlier-version weight-decay results are explicitly not re-examined here and are not included.
record.test_reason: It tracks a basis-explicit progress measure (FSDgen unit agreement) through training on modular multiplication and six finite groups. It asks whether learned structure appears before grokking and whether its timing predicts grokking. This bears on V2's claim that continuous progress measures anticipate the jump. It does not reproduce the original Fourier-circuit measures.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that structure in the task's own basis becomes visible earlier (59/60 multiplication networks), not due to the fixed threshold, and during the plateau at two of three primes. Six groups agree except D16. A lead over grokking is weak evidence because memorisation precedes grokking, and the measure does not predict when a run groks. They make no causal claim.
record.recipe_differences: Uses FSDgen, an answer-averaged activation-profile concentration measure, and controlled basis changes; it does not reproduce the original Fourier-circuit progress measures. The study reports a fixed threshold, an untrained-network null, and equal-rise checks.
record.method_sensitivity: The reading basis affects synchronization timing; fixed-threshold comparisons favor readings with higher untrained scores. Results also vary by task/group and by single-crossing versus 500-step held rules. Equal-rise checks remove the D16 advantage.

fits_no_version.finding: When a progress measure detects structure depends on the reading basis. The task-group basis is reached first, which survives equal-rise thresholds, except on D16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Basis-dependent progress measures register grokking structure earlier in the task group's own basis; wrong bases lag.

fits_no_version.finding: Untrained networks score several times higher than Gaussian noise on the answer-averaged measure, and higher in the right basis.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nulls for progress measures should come from untrained networks; noise nulls overstate early structure.

record.code_released: Scripts and per-run results are stated to be available from the author; no URL is given.
record.problems: Small models and small tasks; one measured layer only; checkpoint intervals are every 100 steps; several analyses, including equal-rise checks and group-family comparisons, were exploratory or added after the sweep. The measure does not establish that the measured structure carries the computation, and the study did not intervene on synchronization. Synchronization time is weakly related to grokking time.
record.rows_left_out: Not included: earlier-rule counts in Table 3, because they concern the unmerged measure and Gaussian null that this version replaces; ideal-layer scores, because they are synthetic diagnostics rather than trained-network synchronization outcomes; and Appendix G top-5 control results, because they concern a superseded comparison measure. The paper’s withdrawn earlier-version weight-decay, addition/subtraction, and ablation analyses are explicitly not re-examined here.

untested.parts: Identification of a generalizing circuit and its causal role; removal of memorizing components. The measured layer may not carry the computation. There is no intervention.
Grokking occurs, but there is no training-set-size sweep of the delay.
No non-algorithmic data or initialization-scale sweep.
Weight-decay results are withdrawn and not re-examined.

missing.what: Memorisation preceded grokking in all 179 grokked runs, by a wider average margin than any synchronisation signal. This is central to judging V2 leads.
Per-task placement of held sync before memorisation / in plateau / after grokking for the groups. S5 10/10/0; Z8×Z9 4/6/10; Z8×Z8 1/15/4.
missing.locator: Table 5 last column; Section 4.3 S5 paragraph

missing.what: Synchronisation-to-grokking gap varied more across seeds than grokking step in 8 of 9 tasks.

record.verdict_notes: Table 3's column headers appear scrambled in the text. The prose confirms held counts of 10 and 16 for Z8×Z9 and Z8×Z8, and Table 4 gives the irreps held counts 20/19/19/19/10/16; the reader used the earlier-rule column for the four abelian rows. Basis-comparison rows were relinked to none because they test measurement basis, not whether progress anticipates grokking. The withdrawn v1 weight-decay and causal results are not treated as findings.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the delayed training-to-test accuracy trajectory as a claim in its own right, or whether reducing training-set size increases the optimization delay. Training fractions are fixed within task family.

Measures FSDgen synchronization, not the formation or causal role of an identifiable generalizing circuit; does not directly measure removal of memorizing components. The timing analyses concern synchronization versus memorization and grokking.
No non-algorithmic datasets or initialization-scale/weight-norm sweep.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning.
No weight-decay or low-norm intervention, critical dataset-size test, or ungrokking test in this version.
Does not compare identifiable algorithms across runs.
Does not test adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax artifact explanations.

relationships.condition: Multiplication p=59, p=97 (discrete-log reading); S5, D16, Z4×Z5, Z5×Z5 (irreps)
relationships.reason: Held synchronisation leads grokking in nearly all runs, mostly inside the memorisation plateau. Rows: M59-D-held 19/20, M97-D-held 17/19, M59-phase 18 plateau, M97-phase 17 plateau, S5-irr, D16-irr, Z4x5-irr, Z5x5-irr.
relationships.display_finding: Sustained synchronization precedes grokking in 19/20 multiplication runs at modulus 59 and 17/19 at modulus 97, with phase synchronization inside the plateau in 18 and 17 runs, respectively, while irreducible-representation measures show similar precursors across the tested groups.
